title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: JAVI'S TAMALES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Javi Soto, a pecan truck driver from Las Cruces, New Mexico.
His best dish? A frozen burrito, still frozen in the middle.
And this Christmas, he had to make six hundred tamales.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE ANNOUNCEMENT
segments.quote: There are only nine meals between mankind and anarchy.
segments.author: Alfred Henry Lewis
lines: For sixty years, his Abuela Chayo made the family's Christmas Eve tamales.
But this fall, at eighty-six, she put down her spoon. My hands are tired, mijo.
Tío Ruben quoted Alfred Henry Lewis, an old newspaper writer:
There are only nine meals between mankind and anarchy.
Everyone laughed. Nobody moved. So Javi raised his hand. I'll do it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE APRON
segments.quote: Cookery is become an art, a noble science; cooks are gentlemen.
segments.author: Robert Burton
lines: His cousins laughed so hard, one snorted horchata.
Abuela handed him her flowered apron and her cookbook.
Inside the cover, she had copied a line from Robert Burton, an old English writer:
Cookery is become an art, a noble science; cooks are gentlemen.
A gentleman in flowers. He took it seriously.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE MUSH
segments.quote: We learn from failure, not from success!
segments.author: Bram Stoker
lines: His first batch came out like wet sand. One slid onto the dog.
He almost quit. Then he remembered a line from Dracula, of all books:
We learn from failure, not from success!
He wrote it down. Too much water. Not enough lard.
The next batch held together. The dog was disappointed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: EVERY NIGHT
segments.quote: First forget inspiration. Habit is more dependable. Habit will sustain you whether you're inspired or not.
segments.author: Octavia Butler
lines: Some nights, after twelve hours driving, he was beat.
His sister Lupe taped a note to his fridge, from the writer Octavia Butler:
First forget inspiration. Habit is more dependable. Habit will sustain you whether you're inspired or not.
Every night, tired or not, he spread masa on a dozen husks.
By December, his hands knew the way.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE DARK
segments.quote: Patience is the best remedy for every trouble.
segments.author: Plautus
lines: Christmas Eve, fifty dozen tamales filled four pots.
Then the power went out on the whole street.
The cousins wanted pizza. Abuela quoted the Roman playwright Plautus:
Patience is the best remedy for every trouble.
Javi moved the pots onto the grill, and they waited in the dark, telling stories. Best hour of the year.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TASTE
segments.quote: What we have once enjoyed we can never lose.
segments.author: Helen Keller
lines: At eight, the lights came back. Abuela took a slow bite.
Too much salt, she said. Just like mine.
She squeezed his hand and quoted Helen Keller:
What we have once enjoyed we can never lose.
Now Javi makes them every year. Abuela is the boss.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Step up. Take it seriously. Learn from the mess. Keep the habit. Be patient. Pass it on.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Step up. Take it seriously. Learn from the mess. Keep the habit. Be patient. Pass it on.
I made tamales once. The fire department still sends me a Christmas card.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
